correctness.rationale: Finding line 14 says a nonconserved zero eigenvalue occurs precisely at a_c. This is false: take L=12, rho=3/4, t=0, a=32r. For m=2, cos(k)=1/2; the Fourier block has exact determinant 0 and trace -22r. Yet a_c=32r/(3 sqrt(3)-2)<32r, and the m=1 block has determinant (480-288 sqrt(3)) r^2<0. There can thus be neutral shorter modes in an already unstable state. Independently derived the blocks from the flow, and checked this counterexample in exact symbolic arithmetic. The determinant divided by positive h is affine increasing for rho>1/2, so the stated first onset, two-dimensional real neutral space at first onset, five-site cutoff, t=0 optimizer and finite-size expansion are otherwise valid. It is the fixed-mass spectral abscissa, not the presence of any zero eigenvalue, that is zero precisely at a_c. Inspected frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py: the sampled growth-rate and root-straddling tests do not check the claimed absence of higher-mode zeros; the uploaded code was not executed.

evidence: On the finite 1D ring the exact 2-by-2 block has negative real trace and det/h=2rA-2C+(AB+C)h. If rho<=1/2 positivity is immediate from the unexpanded sign formula; if rho>1/2 its slope AB+C is positive. Substitute the minimum nonzero h, and the leading activity coefficient is positive exactly if c_L>0 is attainable at some rho<1. At t=0 the density optimization is just maximizing the concave quadratic (1-rho)((1+c_L)rho-1).
